newsitem.title: UK: Paris launch for European air cargo body.
newsitem.headline: Paris launch for European air cargo body.

text.p: The European Air Cargo Forum will be formally launched on March 21 in Paris as an umbrella body to back the needs of the European airfreight industry, European Air Shippers Council (EASC) secretary Chris Welsh said.
The Forum will group shippers, freight forwarders, express carriers and airlines. The decision to set up the body follows discussions with key industry players during the last nine to 12 months.

Welsh, speaking by telephone from Brussels, added that the decision to work towards the Forum was first mooted as one of the recommendations in the EASC's "Airfreight 2000" report issued in September 1995.

However the first detailed talks took place at an exploratory meeting in mid-February between airlines, shippers and express carriers and this disclosed considerable information gaps between the different sides, he said.
"The Forum will also be useful in identifying standards and will help to promote a "best practice" approach for the industry," Welsh said.
Airlines involved in the Forum include KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, Lufthansa Cargo Cargolux, British Airways BAY.L World Cargo, Swisscargo,Aer Lingus, SAS Air France Cargo and Virgin Atlantic.

FreightForward Europe which groups the top European freight forwarders is also involved together with the European Liaison Committee for Freight Forwarders(CLECAT), Welsh added, while MSAS Cargo is an individual member.
Integrators, such as DHL Worldwide Express, Federal Express Corp and United Parcel Service of America are represented via the European Express Organisation(EEO).

The March 21 launch will be preceded by a Paris meeting of the EASC on the previous day, industry sources said. They added the impact of the French government's ban on freight truck movements between 2200 local (2100 gmt on Saturday to the same time on Sundays -- due to come into effect at end-March -- may also be raised at the EASC session.
